title: OpenAI launched a tool this summer that looks exactly like a shot at Wix and Squarespace.

Coach Akinwumi 3 min read · Oct 1, 2026 -- Listen Share OpenAI launched a tool this summer that looks exactly like a shot at Wix and Squarespace. Describe a website, ChatGPT builds it, you get a live link. In the same stretch, OpenAI also launched something else: a partnership that lets Wix build full commercial websites directly inside ChatGPT, through its own app in OpenAI’s directory. OpenAI’s own announcement called it “a great example of the kind of real-world value apps can bring into ChatGPT.” So which is it. Is OpenAI competing with Wix, or partnering with it? Both, and on purpose, because they’re not actually the same bet. Read the fine print on ChatGPT Sites and it’s scoped narrow: no payments, no commerce, not available in the EU yet, explicitly built for internal dashboards and lightweight team tools rather than public business websites. It’s not trying to be Wix. It’s trying to stop ChatGPT Work users from opening a different tab for a quick launch tracker. Meanwhile Wix gets a real storefront inside ChatGPT’s app directory, as part of a broader play where OpenAI is positioning the chat window itself as the front door to other people’s software, and taking a cut of what happens there. That’s a sharper move than “build the competitor” or “partner with the incumbent.” It’s both, at different scopes, aimed at different jobs. Build the narrow internal thing yourself, because owning it keeps people inside your ecosystem. Let the specialist handle the full commercial version, because you don’t need to out-build Wix at e-commerce, you just need Wix to need you. Most leaders treat build-versus-partner as one decision for the whole product. It’s rarely one decision. The real skill is knowing which slice is worth owning outright and which slice is worth collecting rent on instead. Where in your own business are you trying to out-build a partner on something you’d actually be better off just getting a cut of? #Leadership #BusinessStrategy #ManagementLessons #AI Press enter or click to view image in full size The business read, then the files above. This one’s genuinely more nuanced than it looks at first glance. Top voices — Trade coverage and OpenAI’s own announcements carry this story more than independent analysts: SaaS News covering the platform-marketplace mechanics, Playcode’s alternatives roundup doing the sharpest competitive breakdown, and Quiver Quantitative reporting the Wix partnership directly. The actual strategic tension — OpenAI appears to be attacking Wix and Squarespace with its own native website builder. In the same stretch, it also launched a partnership letting Wix build full commercial websites directly inside ChatGPT’s app directory, calling it “a great example of the kind of real-world value apps can bring into ChatGPT.” Those look contradictory until you read the fine print: ChatGPT Sites explicitly bans commerce and payment processing, isn’t available in the EU, and per one reviewer’s assessment, has “a real niche: internal tools for ChatGPT Work teams” — it was never scoped to compete with Wix’s actual business. Meanwhile OpenAI’s broader app-marketplace strategy is explicitly modeled on mobile platform economics: curate a marketplace, embed discovery in the conversational flow, take a cut of what happens there.
